data.name: A Story About My Uncle
data.detailed_description:
A Story About My Uncle (Uma história sobre o meu tio) é um jogo de aventura de plataformas em primeira pessoa sobre um rapaz que procura por seu tio perdido, e acaba em um mundo que ele não poderia nem imaginar que existia. Pegue a ajuda das invenções misteriosas do seu tio que lhe permitem saltar muito alto e distante através de belas paisagens, descubra pistas sobre o paradeiro do seu tio e conheça criaturas fantásticas que irão ajudar-lo na sua jornada.

O movimento na Uma História Sobre O Meu Tio é uma parte crucial de sua jogabilidade – focando no balanceamento pelo mundo com um gancho dando ao jogador uma maravilhosa sensação de velocidade e liberdade. Navega através de um universo de jogo com um estilo de arte única e uma história misteriosa que se desenrola perante ti.

Características principais

  • Gancho de agarrar: Um mecanismo poderoso que dá-te uma sensação de velocidade, fluidez e vertigem, como tu nunca experimentas-te antes.
  • Explora o mundo: Visita um mundo maravilhoso e excitante - de cavernas paradisíacas, até civilizações perdidas e paisagens íngremes e místicas.
  • Ênfase na história: Enquanto procuras pelo teu tio, irás encontrar criaturas com histórias e destinos de si mesmos. Tenha o seu tempo para explorar o mundo e ir mais fundo na narrativa.
  • Não-violento: Uma história sobre o meu tio é um jogo em primeira pessoa, mas é conduzido por uma jogabilidade não-violenta com uma forte ênfase na história e atmosfera.

reviews.review:
[h1]A Story About My Uncle - A Gorgeous Dream That Left Me Feeling Just "Meh"[/h1]
[b]Nostalgia is a funny thing. I remember back in 2017, watching Ducky Bhai play this on one of his classic roasting videos, getting completely hooked by the premise, and buying the game right then and there. It sat in my backlog like a digital artifact until I finally decided to clear it out. I fired it up on my Steam Deck, and credit where it’s due, it runs like an absolute charm on handheld, but once the credits finally rolled, my genuine, honest reaction was just a quiet, resounding "meh."[/b]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1719089223

[h1]A Feast for the Eyes and Ears[/h1]
[b]Let’s give credit where credit is overwhelmingly due, the presentation of [i]A Story About My Uncle[/i] is breathtaking. When you first step into its surreal, floating-island world, it’s hard not to feel a genuine sense of childlike wonder.
The visual design, the dreamy color palette, the whimsical concepts, and the sweeping, atmospheric music combine to create a fairy-tale aesthetic that feels genuinely magical. The animation has this fluid, storybook charm to it, making you feel like you've tumbled right into the pages of a bedtime story told by an adventurous relative. For the first hour or so, the sheer aesthetic beauty and the novelty of swinging around with a high-tech grappling hook had me completely mesmerized.[/b]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3823863687

[h1]Where the Magic Fades[/h1]
[b]Unfortunately, once the honeymoon phase of the gorgeous graphics wears off, the actual game starts to show its seams. The core movement and platforming, swinging through vast chasms using your uncle's inventions, sound incredible on paper. But in practice, the gameplay loop quickly turns into a repetitive cycle of missing jumps, misjudging momentum, and floating back to checkpoints without much genuine engagement.
While the concept of searching for a missing scientist uncle in a hidden civilization sounds like the setup for an unforgettable epic, the execution feels shallow. It lacks the tight, responsive mechanical depth needed to carry a pure first-person platformer. You appreciate what the developers were trying to do, but by the time you reach the end, you realize the style completely overshadowed the substance.[/b]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3824916657

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*][u]Stunning Visual Presentation:[/u] The artistic direction, surreal floating islands, and dreamy world-building are genuinely gorgeous.
[*][u]Wonderful Soundtrack:[/u] The ambient music and audio design completely immerse you in the storybook atmosphere.
[*][u]Flawless Steam Deck Performance:[/u] It runs smoothly, looks crisp, and handles wonderfully on portable hardware.
[*][u]Cozy, Non-Violent Vibe:[/u] A peaceful, stress-free adventure focused purely on exploration and movement.
[/list]
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*][u]Repetitive Gameplay:[/u] The swinging and platforming mechanics lose their novelty halfway through, leading to a dull gameplay loop.
[*][u]Shallow Narrative Execution:[/u] Despite a neat concept, the story and characters fail to leave a lasting emotional footprint.
[*][u]The "Meh" Factor:[/u] Once the initial awe of the graphics wears off, the game struggles to keep you genuinely invested.
[/list]
[h1]Verdict[/h1]
[b][i]A Story About My Uncle[/i] is a fascinating time capsule. Buying it back in 2017 because of a YouTube video felt like discovering a hidden treasure, and experiencing it on the Steam Deck proves how well-optimized it technically is. But a pretty coat of paint and a great soundtrack can only carry a game so far. It’s a nice little indie experiment that looks and sounds like a masterpiece, but plays out as completely average. Worth a look if you want some eye candy on a portable screen, but don't expect it to blow your mind.[/b]
